Original · Unique Research · 2026-05-27

Editor's note: The first-person report and its judgments belong to the original Chinese author. This English rendition retains the opening news hook, the Agent industry context, Singapore's positioning, the full event details, all ten roundtable topics, the confirmed guest list, and the registration instructions. All named companies, products, and people are preserved. Company, personal and product names are transliterated where official English forms remain unverified. Event details and attendee claims are source attributions, not independently verified findings.

Unique Bloom

Global Unique Awards · Singapore

What Kind of AI Agent Has a Real Opportunity to Go Global?

"

Recently, Alibaba Cloud officially announced a batch of new AI products for overseas markets in Singapore: the Agent product MuleRun, the agent programming platform Qoder, the general-purpose desktop agent QoderWork... Alibaba Cloud CTO Li Feifei's judgment is that "overseas market demand for AI continues to be strong, and especially the explosion of Agents has caused model call volume and cloud resource consumption to grow exponentially."

First in April, Anthropic entered the ring itself, releasing the public beta of Claude Managed Agents — a complete framework that lets developers directly build, deploy, and run Agents on the Anthropic platform, pushing a group of startups still laboriously building their own Agent runtime layers straight into a corner. Immediately after, OpenAI updated its own Agents SDK, explicitly taking aim at Anthropic. May's Google I/O went even further, putting "Agentic Gemini" in the spotlight, with Pichai describing the future of AI in the plainest terms — AI is no longer just about answering questions, but about getting work done for people. Now Alibaba Cloud has laid its cards on the table at its own summit: a full-stack Agent-ification upgrade.

Singapore is Southeast Asia's financial, legal, and talent hub, the easiest place for global capital to land in Asia-Pacific, and the most frequent first-stop choice for AI companies going global. A growing number of entrepreneurial teams are setting out from here, extending into Southeast Asia and even the global market.

So the real question arrives: what kind of AI Agent has a real opportunity to go global?

On June 12, we're talking about this in Singapore.

The 2026 Global Unique Awards · Singapore AI Agent Summit (Unique Bloom 2026 · SG AI Agent Summit) will be held on June 12, 2026, 9:00–17:00, at PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering in Singapore.

Led by Unique Research as the main organizer, with co-participation from TMTPost, Canlah.AI, OpenClaw Asia, Yangfan Chuhai (扬帆going overseas), and COCO AI, the summit focuses on the core proposition of AI Agent globalization, and is expected to bring together 500+ global AI industry practitioners, entrepreneurs, and investors.

This is not a general AI discussion. We're only talking about one thing: how AI Agents move from regional to global, from hype to revenue.

One Day, Ten Roundtables, One Theme

The summit agenda revolves around the core path of AI Agent globalization, covering ten topics:

AI Agent globalization: from hype to revenue — is there a real commercialization path?

What kind of AI Agent truly has global capability? Product dimensions, team structure, market selection.

Localization, trust-building, and compliance — required courses for going global; what pitfalls have been stepped in?

What kind of AI Agent startups do investors really want to see — has the valuation logic changed?

The GTM roadmap for AI Agent globalization — how to choose and conquer the first market.

Setting out from Singapore: how to build a global AI Agent company.

Platforms, infrastructure, and ecosystem partners — the key support behind Agent expansion.

A2A: agent collaboration, architecture, and ecosystem — the new paradigm of the multi-agent era.

Autonomous Agents: capability boundaries, security, and governance — the gates to pass before commercialization.

Global deployment of on-device intelligence — from "cloud Agents" to "device Agents."

There is also a special session in the afternoon — the SG AI 30 Awards, recognizing 30 representative teams and products in the Singapore and Asia-Pacific AI ecosystem.

In the evening, a VIP closed-door dinner will be held, where core guests and invited attendees continue in-depth discussion.

Confirmed Attending Guests (Continuously Updating)

Currently confirmed speakers and roundtable guests include:

Agnes AI Founder Bruce Yang (杨通), Emerging AI COO Jolie Li (李卓), zCloak.AI Founder Francis, SOIN AI CEO Sophie Yang (杨婷), ThinkSpace Founder Max Ye, Inflect/Nex Founder Jonathan Liem, BetaAI Co-Founder Yinan Li (李一楠), FizzDragon Founder Zhuo Chen (陈卓), Plaud Head of APAC Marketing Megumi Yoshinaga (吉永恵), AIDX Head of Growth Soh Chin Yih (苏晋毅), SuperIntelligence CEO Kisson Lin, Digitaste Founder Erik Yang, 2nd brain Founder & CEO Hua Mao (毛华), Minipix Founder & CEO Jony Deng, NoDesk AI Founder & CEO Jian Song (宋健), Wavenote Founder & CEO Kun Hua (华琨), VertrAI CEO Wei Xiong (熊炜), COCO AI Co-Founder Charlie Hu, MovieFlow Co-Founder Wei Liang (梁巍), Cuber AI Managing Director C K Ng, Muse AI CEO Jennifer Chen, PingCAP TiDB — APAC AI Business & Product Leader Li Li (李粒), Yuanli Intelligence (元理intelligence) Founder & CEO Fan Zhang (张帆), FOSHO Co-Founder Tony Sun, Shanjian Intelligence (闪剪intelligence) Founder Huapei Yan (严华培), Golden Gate Ventures Managing Partner Jeffrey Paine, Openspace Capital Director & Head of Data Science and AI, PatSnap (wisdom芽) Co-Founder Guan Dian (关典), PlanX CEO Lex.

The guest lineup continues to be confirmed.

Registration Information

Summit attendance is free but requires review. Approved registrants will receive a confirmation email from the organizer.

The organizer will begin reviewing registration information this weekend (May 30–31). Early registration receives priority review. Approved registrants will receive an official confirmation email; upon receiving the confirmation email, you may proceed to attend with confidence.

The registration channel is now open. You may register on the official website: uniquebloom.cn/sg2026

It is now mid-2026. AI Agents have moved from "can it work?" to "how to make money, how to go global."

Singapore happens to stand at this very juncture.

If you're also thinking about this, see you on June 12.
